records.name: Indiana
records.summary: A February 2026 per-state legal-risk assessment placed Indiana 'among the harshest anti-trans states in the country', citing its 2026 identity-document law and escalating bathroom restrictions as the drivers of its adult-risk rating; the July 2026 edition keeps it in the worst-state group.

records.name: Utah
records.summary:
Utah's HB 257 (January 2024) was the first statewide bathroom ban in the country reaching trans adults, not only school facilities; it remains in force, alongside birth-certificate and surgery requirements for amended markers and a complaint channel for objecting officials.

In May 2025 Utah became the first state to explicitly prohibit flying LGBTQ flags at government buildings and schools (fines up to $500 per day), with similar flag bans following in other states — its Pride organisation calls the state's legislative record the nation's most anti-LGBT.

freshness.fact: Jan 30 2024 bathroom law stands (birth-certificate proof, surgery requirement for amended markers) with 2024 complaint channel for officials; no injunction or repeal found on state page.

records.name: North Dakota
records.summary: HB 1259 (2025) facility ban; birth-sex definition in statute. In the worst-law group per the July 2026 legal-risk assessment. Below the national score 0.36.

records.name: South Dakota
records.summary: 2025 facility ban. In the worst-law group per the July 2026 legal-risk assessment. Below the national score 0.36.

records.name: Wyoming
records.summary: Wyoming signed public-facility bans in March 2025. A July 2026 per-state legal-risk assessment lists it among 'the worst states' for legislation targeting transgender adults.

records.name: West Virginia
records.summary: March 2025 facility ban with unusually wide reach: K-12, higher education, corrections and domestic-violence shelters. In the worst-law group per the July 2026 legal-risk assessment. Below the national score 0.36.

records.name: Arkansas
records.summary:
Arkansas confines trans students to birth-sex school facilities under a March 2023 law (HB 1156) that remains in force and was extended in 2025; its school focus means visitor exposure is narrower than in states with adult-reaching bans.

Its ban on gender-affirming care for minors remains in litigation (en-banc review of an injunction reversal pending), and the July 2026 per-state legal-risk grading lists Arkansas among the worst states.

freshness.fact: March 2023 school bathroom law (signed by Gov. Sanders) still in force; care-ban litigation ongoing (en banc review of injunction reversal) - facility claim current.

records.name: Ohio
records.summary:
Ohio enacted a law in 2024 governing public bathroom and facility use by sex assigned at birth, recorded in a national equality tracker of such bans (the tracker's page has since moved from its cited URL).

An independent July 2026 legal-risk assessment of anti-trans legislation lists Ohio among its 'worst states' group for transgender adults, alongside most of the Deep South and several Plains and Mountain states; the same assessment's frame is 'Worst Policies In Effect' nationally.
